Bug_Title: "equals(Object obj)" and "hashCode()" should be overridden in pairs
Bug_Details:
According to the Java Language Specification, there is a contract between equals(Object) and hashCode() :
If two objects are equal according to the equals(Object) method, then calling the hashCode method on each of the two
  objects must produce the same integer result.
It is not required that if two objects are unequal according to the equals(java.lang.Object) method, then calling the hashCode method on each of the two objects must produce distinct integer results.
However, the programmer should be aware that producing distinct integer results for unequal objects may improve the performance of
  hashtables.
In order to comply with this contract, those methods should be either both inherited, or both overridden.
Bug_Explanation: The equals method is overridden but the hashCode method is not. This violates the contract that says if two objects are equal according to the equals(Object) method, then calling the hashCode method on each of the two objects must produce the same integer result. The program may crash if two unequal objects produce the same hash code.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug was triggered by the fact that the equals method was overridden but the hashCode method was not.
